description:
Make a new tool from the Python skeleton, check a tool, or build one step by step. One op per call:
- new: {"op": "new", "path": "my_tools/mul"}  (copies the skeleton: a working tool that adds two numbers; path must not exist yet; relative paths start at your workspace). Optional "description" fills in what the tool does. path may also be FILE.json#/POINTER: the tool goes into that JSON object and its script <name>.py next to the JSON file.
- check: {"op": "check", "path": "my_tools/mul", "sample": {"a": 6, "b": 7}}  (remakes _tooldef.json and _metainfo.json from tool.py, checks them, runs the Example written in the description and tries one call with sample if given; one line per item, lines marked bad say how to fix; the last line says if it is ready)
After new: in tool.py change only the part that new prints (DESCRIPTION, PARAMS, META, run), with edit; do not rewrite the whole file (README.md there has a full example). Then check, then add it: self_tools {"op": "add", "path": "my_tools/mul"}; it works at once: call it by its name in your next reply. path for check can also be a JSON file or FILE.json#/POINTER.
Step by step (a folder, a JSON file or FILE.json#/POINTER): add_entry {"op": "add_entry", "path": "my_func"} writes the entry and a small Python script next to it (a runnable function); add_metainfo {"op": "add_metainfo", "path": "my_func"} then add_tooldef {"op": "add_tooldef", "path": "my_func"} write _metainfo and _tooldef (from the script if it uses tool_spec; otherwise give "description", and for add_tooldef "params": [{"name": "a", "type": "number", "description": "the first number"}]).
Errors: ArgumentsBad, OpUnknown, PathExists (pick another path, or it is already there), PathMissing, ToolBad (see the bad lines). Details: knowledge_read aos/tools.json#/tools_def.

op.description: new = copy the skeleton to a new tool, check = check a tool, add_entry / add_metainfo / add_tooldef = add one part to a folder or JSON object

path.description: new: the new tool folder, or FILE.json#/POINTER (must not exist yet). Other ops: the tool folder, JSON file or FILE.json#/POINTER. Relative to your workspace, or absolute

description.description: new: what the new tool does, with one example call (goes into DESCRIPTION). add_metainfo / add_tooldef: the same, when the script does not use tool_spec

sample.description: check: arguments for one test call, like {"a": 6, "b": 7}

script.description: add_entry: the script's file name next to the entry (default tool.py in a folder, <name>.py for a JSON object); copied from the skeleton if it is not there

meta.description: add_metainfo: only what differs from the defaults, like {"side_effect": true}

params.description: add_tooldef: [{name, type, description, default?, enum?, items?, required?}], type one of string, integer, number, boolean, array, object
